com: I heard a great voice. Bossuet explains the pouring out of the seven vials in this manner. The five first he supposes to have taken place under the reign of Valerian and Gallien; the sixth he supposes to have been poured out during the reigns of Valerian, Dioclesian, and Julian; and the seventh under Honorius and the Alani. (Bossuet) — All commentators, however, seem to agree that the great city mentioned in the 19th verse, is to be understood of Rome, and that the plagues which are here foretold, are denounced against her. (Calmet, Pastorini, &c.) — Go and pour out the seven vials, &c. According to the exposition followed by the bishop of Meaux[Bossuet], all these seven vials are already past, being punishments and judgments exercised against the heathen emperors, from the time of Valerian even to the time of Julian, at whose death it might be said, (ver. 17) it is done. Idolatry is destroyed, as to its public worship. Here in particular, by the drying up of the Euphrates, and by the armies of the East, these interpreters understand those of the Persians, who first gave the great shock to the empire in Valerian’s time, and by whom afterwards Julian the apostate was defeated, and killed. By the great Babylon they also understand idolatrous Rome; and by the islands and mountains sunk by earthquakes, they understand the destruction of divers kingdoms. According to another interpretation, (which is very common) all these judgments are to come before the end of the world; and will be in a manner literally executed about antichrist’s time. At the first vial, men shall be struck with ulcers and wounds, not unlike to the sixth plague of Egypt. At the second and third vial, the sea and fountains shall be turned into blood, as in Egypt. At the fourth vial shall be excessive scorching heats, tormenting men, and burning every thing for their use. At the fifth vial darkness, like that of Egypt. At the sixth vial, (ver. 12.) the Euphrates dried up, to open a passage for the armies from the East, to come and join the forces of antichrist. And the three unclean spirits like frogs, may signify devils sent by the dragon, or chief of the devils, to excite the wicked to all manner of unclean abominations. They are here said to be gathered together in a place called Armagedon, perhaps with an allusion to Mageddon, in the tribe of Manasses, where the two kings of Israel, Ochozias and Josias, perished. (4 Kings ix. 21.) And they are brought in only to signify a place of great destruction. See also Zacharias xii. 11. At the seventh vial, a voice, it is done, i.e. the reign of the wicked in general, and of antichrist, is at an end. (Witham)

And the first. From hence it appears that the first vial was poured out indiscriminately upon the good equally with the wicked. But behold the different consequences that follow: those that have the mark of the beast are afflicted with a sore and grievous wound, which is said in allusion to the madness, fury, and despair with which the wicked were afflicted, whilst St. John’s omitting to say any thing of the just, shews that they bore it with resignation and joy. (Calmet)

And the second. On pouring out the vial follows the divine judgment. There appears blood, like that of a dead man. This passage, Pastorini is of opinion alludes to the Arian heresy, which, like blood, flowed in vigorous circulation whilst in health and strength, gradually retarded its motion, as in a dying man, and was at last totally lost and stopped, like the circulation in a dead man. Hence every living soul died in the sea. (Pastorini) — Calmet interprets it as a prediction of the calamities which befell the Roman empire, during the invasion of the Persians on the east, and the Goths and other barbarous nations on the west.

Upon the rivers. That is, on the Roman provinces in Italy, and Rome itself. This is the last stroke employed by the Almighty for the total destruction of Rome. The divine judgment being executed, the Angel of the waters, that is, the Angel that presided over the Roman states, cries out, (ver. 5, 6.) thou art just, &c. (Pastorini)

And the fourth Angel. Here is the punishment of the Greeks during the siege of Constantinople by the Turks, where the fire engines, that were then made use of for the first time, so reduced the Grecian army, that the walls of the city were reduced to ashes, and the whole town to flames. Hence it appears how the Greeks were scorched with great heat; and how they blasphemed the name of God, appears too evident from the history of Notaros, admiral of the Constantinopolitan fleet. (Pastorini)
Calmet explains this passage of Rome the seat of idolatry, which was given up to the pillage of the barbarians under Alaric. (Calmet)

River Euphrates. That is, a passage is laid open for the potentates of the East to lay their destructive hands upon the countries on this side the Euphrates. For they are the spirits of devils working signs, which are sent forth by the eastern princes, to oblige all to unite in arms against the great day of the Almighty God. (Pastorini)
Armagedon. That is, the hill of robbers. (Challoner)

The seventh vial is poured out upon the air which lies between the earth and the heavens, to indicate that the judgments of God are going to fall upon the whole creation. After which follow these words, it is done. All is over, time is no more; upon which immediately follow lightnings, &c.

Great Babylon came in remembrance before God. The time of God’s punishing the wicked world is approaching: for by a third interpretation, Babylon may signify metaphorically all the wicked in general. (Witham)
And great hail like a talent came down, &c.[1] Which need not be taken literally, but only metaphorically, to signify the heavy weight of God’s judgments upon sinners. (Witham)
Armagedon.... That is, the hill of robbers.
fa: Irenaeus Against Heresies Book 4
AGAINST HERESIES 4.30.4

For the whole exodus of the people out of Egypt, which took place under divine guidance, was a type and image of the exodus of the Church which should take place from among the Gentiles; and for this cause He leads it out at last from this world into His own inheritance, which Moses the servant of God did not [bestow], but which Jesus the Son of God shall give for an inheritance. …
Commentary on Revelation

And I heard a great voice from the temple, saying to the seven angels: Go, and pour out the seven bowls of the wrath of God upon the earth. The voice from the temple is the voice of the Lord commanding the preachers to proclaim the word of God not only to the elect, but also to the wicked, so that the former may have something by which they are corrected, and the latter something by which they are condemned more severely. By “earth,” moreover, sinners are indicated. Therefore the preachers pour out their bowls upon the earth when they announce the word of God to sinners.
Commentary on Revelation

And the first went and poured out his bowl upon the earth, and there came a grievous and very evil sore upon the men who had the mark of the beast, and upon those who worshiped its image. The first angel signifies the preachers who were before the Law, just as the one who in the preceding vision was seen as the first to sound the trumpet (Rev. 8:7). But there, by the third part of the earth that was burned, the elect are signified; here, however, by those who suffered the grievous and very evil sore, the wicked are signified. …
Commentary on Revelation

And the second poured out his bowl into the sea, and it became blood like that of a dead person, and every living soul died in the sea. This angel signifies the teachers of the Law, just as the one who in the prior vision was seen to have sounded the second trumpet (Rev. 8:8-9); but there it is said that a third part of the sea was turned into blood, by which we said the elect were signified; here, however, it is read that the whole sea was turned into blood. The punishment for criminal wickedness according to the Law was the shedding of blood. (Gen. …
Commentary on Revelation

And the third poured out his bowl upon the rivers and upon the springs of waters, and they became blood. This angel signifies the prophets, while by the rivers and the springs of waters the twelve tribes with their families are signified; for even in the preceding vision we said that by the third angel sounding the trumpet the prophets were signified. But there it is read that the third part of the rivers and of the springs was turned into wormwood, (Rev. …
Commentary on Revelation

And I heard the fourth angel saying: You are just, who are, and who were, holy, because you have judged these things; for they poured out the blood of the saints and of the prophets, and you have given them blood to drink, which they are worthy of. By the fourth angel we can understand the angel of that people, who, seeing by the just judgment of God that the wicked people have been condemned, praises the most just sentence of almighty God. And because they poured the blood of the saints and of the prophets, they drank blood; because for the temporal death which they inflicted upon the righteous, they received eternal death.
Commentary on Revelation

And I also heard the altar saying: Lord God almighty, true and just are your judgments. By “the altar” we can understand the holy men who lived at that time, who praised the just judgment of God because He brought most just condemnation upon the wicked people, just as we read that Daniel and the three youths did. (Dan. 3)
Commentary on Revelation

And the fourth poured out his bowl upon the sun, and it was granted to it to scorch men with heat and with fire. And men were scorched with great heat, and they blasphemed the name of God who has power over these plagues; and they did not repent so as to give Him glory. The fourth angel signifies Christ and His apostles, and the other preachers as well, just as we said that the fourth angel in the earlier vision had signified them; (Rev. …
Commentary on Revelation

And men were scorched with great heat. Whoever wishes to know how great that heat was with which the Romans afflicted the Jews, let him read Josephus, and he will find that no nation in all the kingdoms of the earth perished more cruelly (Josephus, The Jewish War, 1.4). And they blasphemed the name of God who has power over these plagues. So wicked was the nation of the Jews that, although they knew they were suffering unheard‑of evils for their crimes, not only did they not cease from their blasphemies against Christ, but in their afflictions they spewed forth even far worse blasphemies against God. …
Commentary on Revelation

And the fifth poured out his bowl upon the throne of the beast, and his kingdom was made dark; and they chewed their tongues for pain, and they blasphemed the God of heaven because of their pains and their wounds, and they did not do penance for their deeds. The fifth angel signifies the orthodox fathers who fought against the heretics, just as we said that the one who, in the earlier vision, sounded the fifth trumpet signified them. (Rev. 9:1-12) And as there the heretics were represented by the locusts, so here the heretics are represented by the throne of the beast; and the beast signifies the Devil. …
Commentary on Revelation

They are also said to have blasphemed God because of their pains and their wounds; for the heretics grieved over the fact that they were always refuted by catholic men; and their wounds were the individual errors of each. Indeed, the heretics blasphemed God because of their pains, because the more they were overcome by catholic men, the greater blasphemies they devised in order to refute them; nonetheless, their own errors, which they professed, drove them on to blaspheme God. They are also said not to have done penance; for you will scarcely find any among the inventors of heresies who has done penance for his errors.
Commentary on Revelation

And the sixth poured out his bowl upon the great river Euphrates, and dried up its water, so that a way might be prepared for the kings from the rising of the sun. This sixth angel has the same meaning as the one who seemed to have sounded the sixth trumpet; (Rev. 9:13) for he signifies the holy martyrs. And those who are there represented by the horsemen, by whom a third part of men is described as having been killed, are in this passage themselves represented by the great river Euphrates, that is, the persecutors of the Church of God. …
Commentary on Revelation

And I saw from the mouth of the dragon and from the mouth of the beast and from the mouth of the false prophet three unclean spirits coming out in the form of frogs; for they are spirits of demons working signs. After describing the calling of the Gentiles, how they came to the faith of Christ, he makes mention of Antichrist, who is to come near the end of the world. …
Commentary on Revelation

And they will go forth to the kings of the whole earth to gather them together for battle on the great day of God Almighty. By the kings of the earth are signified not only kings, but also peoples; now the disciples of Antichrist will gather them together for battle for the great day of God Almighty, not that they would dare to fight against God on the day of judgment, by whom they will be judged so terribly, but they will gather them for battle to persecute the Church, so that on the great day of God Almighty they may be condemned to everlasting punishment. …
Treatise 12. Three Books of Testimonies Against the Jews
Treatise XII Three Books of Testimonies Against the Jews

… Also in the same place: "He who shall overcome I will give him to eat of the tree of life, which as in the paradise of my God. Also in the same place: "Be thou faithful even unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life. Also in the same place: "Blessed shall they be who shall watch, and shall keep their garments, lest they walk naked, and they see their shame. Of this same thing, Paul in the second Epistle to Timothy: "I am now offered up, and the time of my assumption is at hand. I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith. …
Commentary on Revelation

And behold, I come like a thief. The Day of the Lord, as the Apostle says, will come like a thief in the night; for when they shall say, “Peace and security,” then sudden destruction will come upon them. (1 Thess. 5:2–3)
Commentary on Revelation

… Moreover, the garments of our souls are good works: the keeping of the garments is the keeping of the commandments of God. We therefore keep our garments if we fulfill by our deeds what God has commanded. But he is naked who is devoid of good works. The wicked will walk naked when, on the day of judgment, they are led forth empty of good works; and therefore their shame will be seen, because their crimes will be revealed both to angels and to human beings.
Commentary on Revelation

And he will gather them together into the place which in Hebrew is called Armageddon. Armageddon is interpreted as “rounded mountain” or “rising again to former things”; and both interpretations can be applied to the Day of Judgment. For it is rightly called a rounded mountain, because at that time the whole world will be destroyed by balls of fire; and likewise it is rightly called a rising again to former things, because by rising again all human beings will be restored to their former state.
Commentary on Revelation

And the seventh poured out his bowl into the air. By this seventh angel the holy preachers who are to be in the times of Antichrist are signified; just as we have said that he also is meant who above (Rev. 11:15) is read to have sounded the seventh trumpet. By the air, moreover, vain men are signified. Therefore the angel poured out his bowl into the air, because the holy preachers will declare to vain and wicked men that they are to be condemned to everlasting punishment.
Commentary on Revelation

And a great voice went out from the temple from the throne, saying. The great voice is the voice of the holy preachers; by the temple the Church is understood. So a voice went out from the temple, because from the Church the voice of holy preaching proceeds; which is also said to have gone out from the throne, because the Church of God is the throne of God, and, sitting in it, he rests. But what this voice says he makes clear by adding:
Commentary on Revelation
It is done. That is, the end of the world is at hand, in which all things that have been foretold by the Lord and by the saints will be fulfilled.
Commentary on Revelation

And there were flashes of lightning and voices and thunders, and a great earthquake occurred, such as had never been since human beings were upon the earth, such an earthquake, so great. By the flashes of lightning are signified the miracles that God will perform through his saints; for we read above that Elijah and Enoch will work many signs. (Rev. 11:5–6) By the voices is meant the preaching of the saints; and by the thunders the terror of eternal fire is expressed. But the earthquake often signifies the movement of hearts. …
Commentary on Revelation

And the great city was divided into three parts, and the cities of the nations fell. The great city is the city of the Devil, that is, the whole multitude of the wicked: by the three parts into which it is divided, the Jews who refused to believe in Christ, and the pagans, and the false Christians are indicated. But when he says: And the cities of the nations fell, this seems to me to refer to the day of judgment. …
Commentary on Revelation

And great Babylon came into remembrance before God, to give her the cup of the wine of the indignation of His wrath. How is Babylon said to have come into remembrance before God, with whom nothing can be added to or taken away from His remembrance; in whose sight the present, the past, and the future alike stand? But he has put “remembrance” in place of “time. Babylon therefore will come into remembrance before God when that time comes in which He has determined to judge the world and to render to each according to his work. (Rom. …
Commentary on Revelation

And every island fled, and the mountains were not found. The mountains and the islands have the same meaning as the cities of the nations, which a little above are said to have fallen; for by the islands the nations are indicated, and by the mountains their rulers. They are said to flee when they will be destroyed by fire on the day of judgment.
Commentary on Revelation

And great hail, like a talent, fell from heaven upon men. In the Gospel it is written that a certain householder, setting out on a journey, gave to one of his servants five talents, to another two, and to another one. But the first and the second, by trading with the talents which they had received from the lord, doubled them; the third dug in the ground and hid his lord’s money (Matt. 25:15). …
Commentary on Revelation

And men blasphemed God because of the plague of the hail; for it was made exceedingly great. For who in that judgment, so strict and so just, will dare to blaspheme God? But they are said to blaspheme, because the blasphemies of the wicked, which they now hide in their heart, will be revealed to all.
